title: Summer 2027 Assoc AI Engineer Internship
location: Overland Park, KS or Frisco, TX
eligibility: Pursuing a bachelor's in a relevant technical field, with at least one course remaining after the internship; age 18+; authorized to work in the US now and in the future. Existing T-Mobile/Metro employees are excluded from external summer internships.
experience: Coursework or personal projects in AI/ML, Python or Java, and data analysis. Framework, cloud, or certification experience is preferred, not required.
levelReason: The employer explicitly describes an 11-week learning internship and accepts foundational skills demonstrated through coursework or projects.
responsibilities: Help prototype AI-driven customer decision and recommendation workflows.
Test solutions and document findings about reliability and scalability.
Present recommendations while working with cross-functional teams and mentors.
compensation: USD $27–$50 per hour; the posting says actual intern pay depends on education and STEM/non-STEM designation.
portfolio: Prototype a recommendation workflow with synthetic customer records, a simple baseline, 20 fixed test cases, and a short explanation of incorrect recommendations. This is our project suggestion, not the employer's application assignment.

title: 2027 Summer Intern – Machine Learning Engineer, AV/AI Platform
eligibility: Full-time bachelor's or master's student in a relevant STEM field; graduation December 2027–August 2029; at least one term remaining afterward. Twelve weeks at 40 hours/week in one of the stated summer 2027 windows. Office attendance up to three times/week or as the team determines.
experience: Algorithms, data structures, object-oriented programming, and AI/ML coursework, research, or project experience. Distributed systems and accelerator tools are preferred exposure, not all required.
levelReason: Explicit student internship accepting bachelor's/master's candidates and AI/ML experience gained through coursework or projects.
responsibilities: Improve infrastructure for model training, deployment, and inference.
Help optimize data processing, testing, and system monitoring.
Develop code with the team and translate requirements into planned features.
compensation: USD $8,100–$11,800 per month, as advertised for this role; actual offer varies. Eligible students may receive a taxable relocation stipend.
portfolio: Build a small batch-inference pipeline, record latency and throughput before and after one optimization, and document a failed-job recovery test. Keep the project reproducible on modest hardware.

title: Machine Learning Intern, 2027 Summer U.S.
location: Seattle, WA or San Francisco, CA
eligibility: Full-time master's student in a quantitative field, returning to the program after the internship and graduating by August 2028; 12 weeks at 40 hours/week. The posting explicitly excludes F-1/J-1 students and offers no work sponsorship. Must be able to work in Seattle or San Francisco.
experience: Python and software fundamentals plus AI/ML work through coursework, research, or internships. Ability to validate AI-generated code and explain tradeoffs.
levelReason: An explicitly mentored internship, but master's enrollment and work-authorization restrictions make it unsuitable for many undergraduate applicants.
responsibilities: Build and evaluate scoped AI/ML or generative AI projects with mentors.
Run experiments and error analysis on models, retrieval, agents, or evaluations.
Document outcomes, limitations, and implementation tradeoffs.
portfolio: Compare keyword retrieval with an embedding-based search system on a fixed question set; publish error categories, measured results, and cases where the simpler approach works better.

title: Machine Learning Research Intern (Summer 2027)
location: New York, NY or San Francisco, CA
eligibility: Enrolled in a BS, MS, or PhD program focused on ML, deep learning, or NLP, graduating Fall 2027 or Spring 2028; available for a May/June 2027 start in New York or San Francisco. Remote eligibility is not established by the posting.
experience: Prior relevant research experience or publication record and programming experience are required. A previous ML internship and top-venue publications are listed as ideal qualifications.
levelReason: Explicit student internship with mentorship, but it requires prior research evidence. Internship does not mean beginner or no experience.
responsibilities: Investigate model benchmarks, capability measurement, and reliability.
Explore post-training, synthetic data, oversight, or agentic applications.
Improve production models while checking for regressions.
portfolio: Create a small benchmark with a documented scoring rubric, compare two model or prompt versions, and publish a reproducible report analyzing failure cases. Treat this as practice, not a replacement for the required research background.
